extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and peer reviewers (study section members), research administrators
extracted.subtask_short: nih peer review for research grants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on NIH peer review process and review criteria for evaluating research grant applications (R01/R03/R21), intended for study section members and applicants preparing submissions. Covers core scored criteria, overall impact, scoring mechanics, procedural rules, and changes to applications and ESI policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this study address an important problem? If the aims of the application are achieved, how will this advance scientific knowledge? What will be the effect of this study on the concepts or methods that drive this field?

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the conceptual framework, design, methods, and analyses adequately developed, well integrated, and appropriate to the aims of the project? Does the applicant acknowledge potential problem areas and consider alternative tactics? For applications designating multiple Project Directors/Principal Investigators (PDs/PIs), is the leadership approach, including the designated roles and responsibilities, governance and organizational structure consistent with and justified by the aims of the project and the expertise of each of the PDs/PIs?

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project employ novel concepts, approaches or methods? Are the aims original and innovative? Does the project challenge existing paradigms or develop new methodologies or technologies?

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigators
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PI(s) and other key personnel appropriately trained and well suited to carry out this work? Is the work proposed appropriate to the experience level of the PD/PI(s) and other researchers? Do the PD/PI(s) and investigative team bring complementary and integrated expertise to the project (if applicable)?

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Do(es) the scientific environment(s) in which the work will be conducted contribute to the probability of success? Does the proposed study benefit from unique features of the scientific environment or subject populations, or employ useful collaborative arrangements? Is there evidence of institutional support?

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the five core review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overall impact is not a 6th review criterion and is not necessarily the arithmetic mean of the scores for the scored review criteria. It is the synthesis/integration of the five core review criteria that are scored individually and the additional review criteria which are not scored individually. Likelihood (probability) is primarily derived from the investigator(s), approach and environment criteria. Sustained powerful influence is primarily derived from the significance and innovation criteria. Reviewers are encouraged to identify the research field(s) they believe will be influenced by the project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (fellowship applications)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fellowship applications: overall impact should reflect likelihood that the fellowship will enhance the candidate’s potential for, and commitment to, a productive independent scientific career in a health-related field.

rubrics_metrics.name: 9‑point rating descriptors and weakness definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Impact Score Descriptor mapping 1–9 to qualitative descriptors (e.g., 1 Exceptional: Exceptionally strong with essentially no weaknesses; 2 Outstanding: Extremely strong with negligible weaknesses; 3 Excellent: Very strong with only some minor weaknesses; ... up to 9 Poor: Very few strengths and numerous major weaknesses).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional guidance on strengths/weaknesses: Minor Weakness = An easily addressable weakness that does not substantially lessen impact. Moderate Weakness = A weakness that lessens impact. Major Weakness = A weakness that severely limits impact. Reviewers should use the entire rating scale routinely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑numeric score options
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-numeric score options available to reviewers: NR = Not Recommended for Further Consideration, DF = Deferred, AB = Abstention, CF = Conflict, NP = Not Present, ND = Not Discussed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring calculation and final score range
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall impact/priority scores for discussed applications will be the mean of scores voted by all eligible reviewers, multiplied by 10. Final scores will range from 10–90, in whole numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final scores are posted to the applicant’s eRA Commons account within a few days of the meeting; summary statements are compiled by the SRO and released about two months later. Reviewers may modify critiques and associated criterion scores in IAR after the study section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percentiling rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Scores are percentiled to the appropriate base (e.g., the study section base if there are >25 R01 applications or a CSR-all or IC-all base if <25). A percentile ranks your application relative to other applications reviewed by your study section at its last three meetings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percentiles range from 1 to 99 in whole numbers. All percentiles are rounded up to a whole number (e.g., 10.1 becomes 11). A lower percentile number indicates a better score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion scores not discussed by the committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedure: Assigned reviewers discuss strengths and weaknesses and recommend an overall impact/priority score. Criterion scores (the individual scored review criteria) are not discussed by the committee as part of the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study section roles and discussion procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: At the study section: proposals are presented (usually in order of highest average score to worst). There are primary, secondary and tertiary reviewers. The primary gives an overview/summary; secondary adds what the primary missed (asked to avoid duplication); tertiary often does not speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chair moderates discussion, describes triage process, and can keep discussion on schedule. Chair asks for all scores; final scores are given by primary, secondary, and tertiary, then the chair states the expected score range and asks if anyone will vote outside that range (justification required if voting outside the range). Better proposals generally have less discussion; middle and poor proposals get more discussion. Do not discuss proposals outside the meeting; recusals for conflicts are enforced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internet‑Assisted Review (IAR) pre‑review process
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers use eRA Commons to choose Internet-Assisted Review (IAR) to download material. IAR allows critique and preliminary score submission and modification, acceptance of critiques in Word (*.doc) or plain text (*.txt) format, streamline voting, and electronic posting of additional meeting materials for reviewers to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application structure and length changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Strategy section replaces Background and Significance, Preliminary Data, and Research Design and Methods sections. Biosketch and Resources sections have changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page limits: 12 pages for R01 research strategy; 6 pages for R03/R21 research strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: New and Early Stage Investigator (ESI) policies (phased implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: NOT-OD-09-013: For FY2009, NIH expects to support New Investigators at success rates equivalent to established investigators submitting new applications. NOT-OD-08-121: New Investigators within ten years of completing their terminal research degree or within ten years of completing their medical residency will be designated Early Stage Investigators (ESIs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOT-OD-09-021: All New Investigators must update their eRA Commons profiles to ensure appropriate consideration for R01 applications; degree date and residency completion date will be used to determine ESI eligibility. NOT-OD-09-034: NIH will consider requests to extend the ESI period to accommodate lapses in research or part-time periods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation Plan priorities for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH stated priorities for enhancing peer review: Priority 1 – Engage the Best Reviewers; Priority 2 – Quality & Transparency of Review; Priority 3 – Provide Balanced and Fair Reviews Across Scientific Fields and Career Stages; Priority 4 – Continuous Review of Peer Review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority 1: recruit and retain accomplished, broad-thinking, creative scientists. Priority 2: strive for maximum clarity, fairness, consistency; focus on potential impact, originality, and feasibility. Priority 3: fairly evaluate proposals regardless of career stage or discipline and avoid bias toward conservative approaches at expense of innovation. Priority 4: develop a permanent process for continuous quality control and improvement of peer review, including data-driven evaluation and peer review pilots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals of the changes to review (NIH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stated goals: Clearer understanding of the basis of application ratings; More emphasis on impact and less emphasis on technical details; Succinct, well-focused critiques that evaluate, rather than describe, applications; Routine use of the entire rating scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines and critique template availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed guidelines for reviewers and critique templates are provided by NIH (links cited: reviewer_guidelines.htm and CMS/PeerReviewMeetings reviewer guidelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH reviewer guidelines and example R01 review in handout for critique template and case studies.
